hints.content:
To find the average rate of change $(ARC)$ of the function $f$ over the interval $-7 \leq x \leq 2$, we need to take the total change in the function value over the interval (which is the difference of its values at the endpoints) and divide it by the length of the interval:

 $ARC_{-7\leq x \leq 2}= \dfrac{f(2)-f(-7)}{2-(-7)}$.

Note that this is the same as finding the slope of the line connecting the points on the graph that correspond to the endpoints of the interval:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The graph is a continuous curve that contains the following points: the point negative seven, negative seven, the point negative five, negative five, the point negative two, five, the point zero, eight, the point two, five, the point five, negative five, and the point seven, negative seven. The point negative seven, negative seven and the point two, five are connected a solid line segment. There is a dashed segment from negative seven, negative seven to two, negative seven. There is another dashed segment from two, negative seven to two, five.

hints.content:
According to the graph, $f(\blue{-7})=\pink{-7}$ and $f(\blue{2})=\pink{5}$. Therefore, the average rate of change we are looking for is:

$\dfrac{\pink{5}-(\pink{-7})}{\blue{2}-(\blue{-7})}=\dfrac{12}{9}=\dfrac{4}{3}$.
